 1          Pursuant to Rule 26(f) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Local Rule 16-9, the Court’s

 2 Order Setting Initial Case Management Conference and Deadlines, and this Court’s Standing Orders,

 3 Plaintiffs Elizabeth Shipley and Shaun Herod (“Plaintiffs”) and Defendants Meta Platforms, Inc. and

 4 Meta Platforms Technologies, LLC (“Meta” or “Defendants,” and collectively with Plaintiffs, the

 5 “Parties”) respectfully submit the following joint case management statement. In compliance with

 6 Rule 26(f), counsel for the respective Parties met and conferred via Zoom on September 30,

 7 2025. The Parties set forth their position(s) on the following issues.

 8          1.      JURISDICTION AND SERVICE

 9          Parties’ Joint Statement. Plaintiffs allege that this Court has subject matter jurisdiction

10 pursuant to the Class Action Fairness Act, 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d)(2). The amount in controversy,

11 Plaintiffs allege, exclusive of costs and interest, exceeds the sum of $5 million in the aggregate.

12 Plaintiffs allege there are over 100 members of the proposed Classes that are known to exist. Plaintiffs

13 further allege that at least one of the members of the proposed Classes is a citizen of a different state

14 than Defendants.

15          All parties have been served. Venue is proper in this judicial district pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §

16 1391. The Parties agree that there are no issues with personal jurisdiction at this time; nor are there

17 issues with service of process.

18          2.      FACTS
19          Plaintiffs’ Statement. Plaintiffs bring this action on behalf of consumers (nationwide, in

20 California, and in New York) who purchased Meta Portal, Portal+, Portal TV, or Portal Go devices

21 (“Meta Portal devices”). Plaintiffs allege that Defendants launched the Meta Portal as a smart display

22 and video calling device in 2018, and over time, that Defendants rolled out four different models

23 within the Meta Portal product line: the Meta Portal, Portal+, Portal TV, and Portal Go. First Am.

24 Compl. ¶ 12, ECF No. 18 (“FAC”). The Meta Portal devices came equipped with numerous software

25 applications, including videochatting applications such as Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, Zoom,

26 Facebook Live; workplace connectivity applications, including Workplace Live and Microsoft Teams;

27 the “Hey Portal” voice command integrated through Amazon’s Alexa function; music streaming

28 services through applications like Spotify, Pandora, iHeartRadio, Tidal Music; video streaming through
                                                       1
                                     JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                         CASE NO. 3:25-CV-03324-WHO
      Case 3:25-cv-03324-WHO           Document 30        Filed 10/15/25      Page 3 of 12



 1 Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Showtime, CBS News, and ESPN; “Story Time”; a digital photo and

 2 video slideshow frame; special effects, such as background effects and masks available on Facebook

 3 Messenger video calls; and the Calendar and Microsoft Intune functions. Id. ¶¶ 13, 21. Plaintiffs allege

 4 that Defendants knew that access to these applications was important to consumers, but in spite of

 5 their promises that the Meta Portal devices would work with various “trusted apps,” they announced

 6 in December 2022 that they would discontinue development and sale of the Meta Portal devices. Id.

 7 ¶¶ 13, 19-20. Soon after, they unilaterally began removing nearly every application it had advertised,

 8 as well as voice functionality, in early 2025, removing or soon planning to remove Zoom, Amazon

 9 “Alexa” voice assistant, “Hey Portal” voice assistant (all voice functionality), Facebook Live,

10 Workplace Live, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Intune, Spotify, StoryTime, Pandora, iHeartRadio, Tidal

11 Music, Deezer, SideChef, BlueJeans, GoToMeeting, Webex, Red Bull TV, Watch Together, Facebook

12 Watch, The Calendar, CCBS News, ESPN, Photo Booth, background effects and masks on Messenger

13 video calls, and the MetaPortal App. Id. ¶¶ 19-21, 25. Plaintiffs allege that Defendants’ unilateral

14 decision to discontinue consumer access to these advertised applications (in other words, their

15 “bricking” of the Meta Portal devices), significantly less useful to consumers. Id. ¶¶ 25-26.

16          Defendants’ Statement. In 2018, Meta launched the Portal, a smart display and video calling

17 device that offered a variety of first- and third-party applications (the “Applications”) to consumers,

18 including applications with video-calling and music and video streaming capabilities. Some of the
19 Applications and features on the Portal require on-going technical and software support from Meta

20 to function. The Portal came with a one-year limited consumer warranty from Meta (the

21 “Warranty”). In the Warranty, Meta promised to “make and keep software and services available” on

22 the Portal during the one-year Warranty Period . In the Supplemental Terms of Service, which

23 were made available to users when they first activated their devices, Meta reserved the right to “impose

24 limits on, suspend, eliminate, change or update certain existing features” on the devices. Meta also

25 disclaimed all implied warranties in the Warranty and the Supplemental Terms of Service.

26          Plaintiff Shipley purchased her Portal device in November 2020 directly from Meta. Plaintiff

27 Herod purchased his Portal and Portal TV devices in or around March 2022 from Best Buy. While

28 Plaintiffs allege they purchased their Portal devices after “being exposed to” online or TV
                                                     2
                                   JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                       CASE NO. 3:25-CV-03324-WHO
      Case 3:25-cv-03324-WHO           Document 30        Filed 10/15/25      Page 4 of 12



 1 advertisements, Plaintiffs do not identify a single, specific advertisement or statement either of them

 2 saw (let alone relied upon) prior to purchasing their Portal devices.

 3          Although Meta had hoped the Portal would be a commercial success, unfortunately that was

 4 not the case. In late 2022, Meta made the decision to discontinue the Portal due to its market

 5 performance. As it began the process of phasing out the Portal, Meta provided notice to customers

 6 in mid-2023 that it would continue to provide full software support for core Applications on the Portal

 7 until at least January 31, 2025, when it would begin to phase out software support for the device. In

 8 other words, Meta continued maintaining software support for these Applications for at least two

 9 years after it discontinued the device. By January 31, 2025, Ms. Shipley had owned and used her Portal

10 for more than four years and Mr. Herod had owned and used his Portal devices for nearly three

11 years—far exceeding the Warranty period for both Plaintiffs. Plaintiffs do not deny that for the years

12 preceding the phaseout (and the entirety of the one-year warranty), they each had access to an array

13 of Applications originally available on the Portal.

14          On April 14, 2025, Plaintiffs filed this lawsuit, alleging that Meta failed to disclose the

15 possibility that it would stop providing software support for the Portal and asserting a host of false

16 advertising, consumer protection, and even computer hacking claims. Plaintiffs’ allegations cannot

17 survive a motion to dismiss, which Meta filed on August 7, 2025.

18          Even if Plaintiffs’ case were to survive a motion to dismiss, Plaintiffs will not be able to

19 establish that the requirements of Rule 23 have been satisfied such that a class should be

20 certified. Defendants believe that discovery will reveal several issues that render the case improper

21 for class treatment, including, without limitation, that a whole host of individualized issues prevent

22 common issues from predominating, including the circumstances of how each putative class member

23 lost access to any of the applications and features at issue, which disclosures each putative class

24 member received and viewed, and whether and how much each putative class member valued the

25 applications and features at issue.

26          3.      LEGAL ISSUES

27          Parties’ Joint Statement. The legal issues in this case will include, among others: (1) whether

28 Plaintiffs have adequately pled each of their claims; (2) whether the proposed action can be maintained
                                                     3
                                   JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                       CASE NO. 3:25-CV-03324-WHO
      Case 3:25-cv-03324-WHO           Document 30         Filed 10/15/25       Page 5 of 12



 1 as a class action (including whether the proposed Class meets the requirements of Rule 23(a), (b)(2),

 2 and (b)(3)); (3) whether Defendants are liable under any of the claims alleged in the First Amended

 3 Class Action Complaint; and (4) whether Plaintiffs are entitled to any damages, restitution,

 4 disgorgement, declaratory, injunctive and/or equitable relief as alleged in the First Amended Class

 5 Action Complaint.

 6          4.      MOTIONS

 7          Parties’ Joint Statement. Defendants moved to dismiss the First Amended Class Action

 8 Complaint. Defendants’ Motion has been fully briefed and will be heard by this Court on October 22,

 9 2025.

10          Plaintiffs’ Statement. Plaintiffs anticipate filing a motion for class certification prior to the

11 completion of discovery and a motion for summary judgment after discovery is completed. Plaintiffs

12 further anticipate filing motions to exclude Defendants’ experts under Federal Rule of Evidence 702.

13          Defendants’ Statement. Should Plaintiffs’ First Amended Class Action Complaint survive the

14 Motion to Dismiss, Defendants intend to oppose Plaintiffs’ motion for class certification and, if

15 applicable, file a Daubert motion to exclude Plaintiffs’ class certification expert by October 9, 2026, as

16 outlined in the proposed case schedule below in Section 15. Defendants also anticipate bringing a

17 motion for summary judgment, including, without limitation, on issues of liability and damages.

18          5.      AMENDMENT OF PLEADINGS AND ADDITION OF PARTIES
19          Plaintiffs’ Statement. At this time, Plaintiffs do not anticipate adding any new parties to the

20 case. Plaintiffs may seek leave to add additional plaintiffs/class representatives during the time

21 permitted for amendments to the pleadings.

22          Defendants’ Statement. Defendants are unaware of additional parties at this time. Per Fed.

23 R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2), and as Plaintiffs have acknowledged in their statement above, Plaintiffs are required

24 to seek Defendants’ written consent or the court’s leave to make any further amendments to their

25 First Amended Class Action Complaint.

26          6.      EVIDENCE PRESERVATION

27          The Parties have reviewed the Guidelines Relating to the Discovery of Electronically Stored

28 Information (“ESI Guidelines”) and have met and conferred pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)
                                                      4
                                    JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                        CASE NO. 3:25-CV-03324-WHO
      Case 3:25-cv-03324-WHO             Document 30      Filed 10/15/25      Page 6 of 12



 1 regarding reasonable and proportionate steps taken to preserve evidence relevant to the issues

 2 reasonably evident in this action.

 3          7.      INITIAL DISCLOSURES

 4          The Parties will exchange Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures on November 12, 2025.

 5          8.      DISCOVERY

 6                  A.       Status of Discovery

 7          Parties’ Joint Statement. No formal discovery has been conducted to date and no discovery

 8 deadlines have been established. The Parties have agreed to focus precertification discovery efforts

 9 on class certification issues, with the Parties reserving their right to conduct certain “clean up”

10 discovery following a ruling on class certification. The Parties agree that such “clean up” discovery is

11 intended to be limited in scope and will continue to confer regarding the scope of such discovery. The

12 Parties agree any remaining fact discovery will be completed one month after the Court issues its

13 ruling on Plaintiffs’ class certification motion.

14                  B.       Scope of Discovery

15          Plaintiffs’ Statement. Plaintiffs anticipate seeking documents and written discovery from

16 Defendants relating to: Defendants’ marketing of the Meta Portal devices, including marketing relating

17 to the applications that will be available to Meta Portal device users and the functionality of the Meta

18 Portal devices, and any market research regarding the same; Defendants’ decision to omit at point-of-
19 sale that it could and would unilaterally disable any and all applications available on the Meta Portal

20 devices; Defendants’ decision to discontinue the development and sale of the Meta Portal devices;

21 Defendants’ contracts over time with third parties regarding the applications available; Defendants’

22 decision to discontinue Meta Portal device users’ access to applications that had been available on the

23 Meta Portal devices; complaints to Defendants regarding the discontinuation of applications; net and

24 gross sales of the Meta Portal devices; and any contact information in Defendants’ possession for the

25 Proposed Classes.

26          Defendants’ Statement. To the extent Plaintiffs’ First Amended Class Action Complaint

27 survives Defendants’ Motion to Dismiss, Defendants anticipate seeking documents and written

28 discovery from Plaintiffs relating to their experience with their Meta Portal devices, including but not
                                                      5
                                    JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                        CASE NO. 3:25-CV-03324-WHO
      Case 3:25-cv-03324-WHO            Document 30         Filed 10/15/25        Page 7 of 12



 1 limited to: Plaintiffs’ exposure to and understanding of Defendants’ marketing and advertising of the

 2 Meta Portal devices; Plaintiffs’ purchase of their Portal devices; Plaintiffs’ knowledge and

 3 understanding of the Portal’s one-year Warranty and Supplemental Terms of Service; Plaintiffs’ use

 4 and enjoyment of the Portal device and its features; Plaintiffs’ knowledge and experience regarding

 5 Meta’s phaseout of the applications available on the Portal; Plaintiffs’ communications with Meta

 6 about the Portal; and Plaintiffs’ alleged damages incurred as a result of Meta’s discontinuation of the

 7 Portal and phaseout of the applications available on the Portal.

 8                  C.      Limitations or Modifications of the Discovery Rules

 9          Parties’ Joint Statement. The Parties do not currently propose any changes to the limitations

10 on discovery or discovery schedule provided by the Court, the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, or

11 Local Rules. The Parties reserve their rights to seek further modifications to limits on discovery.

12                  D.      Protective Order

13          Parties’ Joint Statement. The Parties anticipate submitting a stipulated protective order

14 regarding the confidentiality and protection of discovery in this action.

15                  E.      Electronic Discovery

16          Parties’ Joint Statement. The Parties met and conferred pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f) and

17 discussed the Court’s Guidelines Relating to Discovery of Electronically Stored Information. The

18 Parties anticipate submitting a stipulated ESI Protocol that will apply to discovery in this matter.
19                  F.      Issues About Claims of Privilege

20          Parties’ Joint Statement. The Parties propose that any disclosure of privileged material will be

21 governed by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(b)(5)(B), Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) and the

22 terms of the protective order to be agreed upon by the Parties.

23          9.      CLASS ACTIONS

24          Parties’ Joint Statement. Counsel for the Parties have reviewed the Procedural Guidance for

25 Class Action Settlements.

26          Plaintiffs’ Statement. Plaintiffs intend to file a motion for class certification. Plaintiffs seek to

27 represent the following Classes:

28

                                        CASE NO. 3:25-CV-03324-WHO
      Case 3:25-cv-03324-WHO            Document 30        Filed 10/15/25       Page 8 of 12



 1           Nationwide Class: All persons who reside in the United States who purchased a Meta
             Portal device.
 2           California Class: All persons who reside in California who purchased a Meta Portal
             device.
 3           New York Class: All persons who reside in New York who purchased a Meta Portal
             device.
 4

 5           This action is properly maintained as a class action under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(a)

 6 and (b) as alleged in the First Amended Complaint. See FAC ¶¶ 49-57.

 7           Defendants’ Statement. Meta disputes that this action is maintainable on a class-wide basis

 8 and opposes certification of the putative classes Plaintiffs seek to represent.

 9           10.     RELATED CASES

10           Parties Joint Statement. The Parties are not aware of any related cases or proceedings at this

11 time.

12           11.     RELIEF

13           Plaintiffs’ Statement. Plaintiffs seek an order certifying the proposed Class and an order

14 awarding full restitution during the applicable statute of limitations, pre and post judgment interest,

15 the cost of the suit herein, and attorneys’ fees. Plaintiffs have not yet performed a computation of

16 restitution in this case and will request documents in discovery to do so.

17           Defendants’ Statement. Meta’s position is that Plaintiffs are not entitled to any relief, this

18 action cannot be maintained on a class-wide basis, and that the entire action should be dismissed with
19 prejudice.

20           12.     SETTLEMENT AND ADR

21           Parties’ Joint Statement. No settlement discussions have occurred at this time. The Parties

22 agree that private mediation is the preferred ADR process, but believe it is premature to engage in

23 ADR or settlement discussions at this time.

24           Per ADR L.R. 3-5, the Parties have read the handbook entitled “Dispute Resolution

25 Procedures in the Northern District of California,” available at www.adr.cand.uscourts.gov.

26           13.     OTHER REFERENCES

27           Parties’ Joint Statement. At present, the Parties do not believe that this case is suitable for

28 reference to binding arbitration, a special master, or the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation.

 2            Parties’ Joint Statement. At present, the Parties are not aware of any issues that can be

 3 narrowed at this time. However, the Parties reserve their right to narrow issues, by agreement, where
